messages:
Maya (Sales): Heads up: POC customer 'HelioTech' hit repeated 429s during a bulk embeddings import. Demo in 4 hours. Need quick triage and a short-term safety net. acct:HEL-77.

Evan (SE): Which endpoint and their QPS pattern? Any response headers?

Maya (Sales): /v1/embeddings. They reported spikes ~60 rps with lots of single-row requests. Response had X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and body 'per_route_cap'.

Sam (Infra): per_route_cap means route-level reservation burned. Account-level quota still ok. Likely because they didn't batch and used many concurrent workers. Two options: reduce client concurrency or grant temporary per-route credits.

Evan (SE): Can we do a fast temporary reservation for the route while we coach them on batching?

Ruth (Oncall): I can apply +250 rps to /v1/embeddings for HEL-77 for 6 hours. I'll also enable granular logging for the session to check noisy neighbors. Apply now?

Maya (Sales): Please apply. I'll tell the customer immediately. They want confirmation text for the demo.

ops-bot: Temporary reservation applied: +250 rps to route "/v1/embeddings" for acct:HEL-77 until 2109880743. Ticket: PR-9932.

Evan (SE): For the customer: recommend batching up to 64 items per call and exponential backoff on 429s. Quick client snippet in Go: "if status==429 { sleep(backoff) }". Also we should add a note to the POC checklist about reserving per-route credits for bulk imports.

Sam (Infra): Post-demo follow-ups: 1) add a small trial reservation product (opt-in), 2) improve docs on batching vs per-route accounting, 3) add SDK quickstart showing batch usage for imports. I'll draft a proposal.

Maya (Sales): Demo team confirmed import succeeded after the reservation. Please keep the ticket open for 24h smoke tests. I'll coordinate customer messaging. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
